answer: Proof-of-stake protocols enforce Sybil resistance by requiring agents to lock capital, creating an ocean of liquidity that validates network integrity. An attacker attempting to flood the system faces a comet-like trajectory toward financial ruin, as the cost of acquiring sufficient stake exceeds the projected gains. This economic barrier ensures any malicious action triggers a ripple effect of penalties, effectively marginalizing fake identities while maintaining decentralized security through verifiable asset commitment.
